messages:
maya: handing off — been noodling on the streaming/regression that started ~2h ago. root cause looks like a burst in Dedicated pool -> fallback cascade to CPU-backed variants, which caused a few hundred 502/504s for streaming endpoints in us-east. I mitigated by toggling routing to prefer warm pools and pinning a couple of heavy flows to the 'stable-v1' model. open ticket: INC-834 (created). leaving notes below, please take over.

maya: what I did:
- increased dedicated pool capacity + bumped autoscale min by 1 instance (temp)
- pinned `/v1/models/stable-v1` for high-throughput routes
- disabled the aggressive fallback rule (policy: fallback-if-latency>200ms) to prevent immediate cascade
- kicked KV cache reclaim on a few hosts that were near memory pressure (see opsbot logs)
- filed INC-834 and added initial customer-impact list (see katie msg)

maya: primary for next 6h = liam, secondary = nora. zane on-call for infra escalations.

liam: ack. taking primary. quick Q: are rolling restarts still in flight?

maya: no rolling restarts currently. I held all deploys for the lane. there are a couple of hosts still under high load but not restarting.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT INC-834 | hosted-api streaming regressions | severity: P2 | pages sent: 3 | link: https://pager.redwood/inci/INC-834

opsbot: logs & recent ops actions: https://ops.redwood/logs?query=INC-834 | host-summary: host-12, host-21 showed KV evictions at ~11:23UTC. memory pressure triggered GC spikes.

zane: saw the KV cache thrash earlier. looks like retention window got shorter after a gc cycle. I can take a look at the kernel-level OOM hints if you want.

liam: yes please, zane — if you can check max_map_count and dmesg for OOM_kill patterns. also can you confirm whether the fallback path is CPU-quantized model causing big token-processing lag?

zane: will check. early quick check: dmesg shows a lot of 'page_alloc' warnings around the time. no OOM_kill yet. max_map_count is normal.

meera: customer impact: which endpoints/customers? we should notify CS.

katie: short list from the initial runbook scrape: acme-inc (critical), bolt-ai (medium), edu-labs (low). roughly 4% of token volume in the last 30m went to fallbacks; affected streaming sessions were the most visible. I pinged CS with a heads-up.

liam: good. I'll prepare a short customer-facing blurb once we have timeline.

nora: runbook pointers for whoever picks this up later: runbooks/runbook-streaming-degrade.md — steps 3/4 to check routing policies, 6 for cache reclaim. also runbooks/autoscale-tuning.md for temp scale overrides.

liam: action items from my side:
- (A1) monitor error-rate and p95/p99 for streaming (primary) — ongoing
- (A2) create temp PR to relax fallback threshold from 200ms -> 350ms (if ops agrees) — will file shortly
- (A3) open follow-up ticket for autoscale policy review (postmortem item) — created: TKT-2047

maya: assigning A1 to liam, A2 to nora (please review before merge), A3 I'll own with product.

liam: quick check command I'm running for health probes:
```
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood/v1/health/streaming | jq .status
```

nora: I'll review the PR now. if we relax fallback threshold we should also add a temporary rate cap on the heavy route to avoid re-triggering the problem.

zane: infra follow-ups I propose:
- check kernel page reclaim settings across the pool
- add a short-lived eviction guard that delays cache pruning during rapid bursts
- instrument per-host GC timings more finely (short term)
I'll open infra-TKT-88.

meera: scheduling: can we get a brief post-handoff sync in 1 hour to confirm stability?

liam: yes — +1 hour. will post a status update in this thread before the sync.

maya: one more thing — I left a runbook fragment in INC-834 with the exact commands I ran for cache reclaim and the temporary routing override. link: https://inc.redwood/INC-834#actions

katie: CS update sent: "We saw brief streaming interruptions for a small subset of customers in us-east. Our engineering team mitigated by routing to stable models and scaling capacity. A follow-up will be provided after investigation."

liam: update 15m later: error-rate down ~70%, streaming p99 improved from 820ms -> 260ms after the temporary scale and pin. Continued monitoring.

nora: reviewed PR and left one comment about adding the rate cap config.

maya: thanks all. handoff notes summary in one line for the rotation: liam primary, nora secondary, zane infra; mitigation = scale up + pin stable-v1 + disable aggressive fallback; follow-ups: TKT-2047 (autoscale review), infra-TKT-88, postmortem scheduled.

liam: closing note: I'll file the retro invite for 1 day from now with SLO owner and product. link to tentative calendar: https://cal.redwood/meet/retro-INC-834

oncall-bot: handoff recorded: primary=liam, secondary=nora, notes attached.

maya: thanks — passing badge to you liam. ping if anything spikes. :thumbsup:
